solution: Let \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \cos^2 x\,dx\). By \(\int_{0}^{a} f(x)\,dx = \int_{0}^{a} f(a-x)\,dx\), \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \cos^2\!\left(\tfrac{\pi}{2}-x\right)dx = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin^2 x\,dx\). Adding, \(2I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2}(\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x)\,dx = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} 1\,dx = \tfrac{\pi}{2}\), so \(I = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\).

Let \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \dfrac{\sqrt{\sin x}}{\sqrt{\sin x} + \sqrt{\cos x}}\,dx\). Using \(\int_{0}^{a} f(x)\,dx = \int_{0}^{a} f(a-x)\,dx\) with \(a = \tfrac{\pi}{2}\) (so \(\sin x \leftrightarrow \cos x\)), \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \dfrac{\sqrt{\cos x}}{\sqrt{\cos x} + \sqrt{\sin x}}\,dx\). Adding, \(2I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} 1\,dx = \tfrac{\pi}{2}\), so \(I = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\).

Let \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \dfrac{\sin^{3/2} x}{\sin^{3/2} x + \cos^{3/2} x}\,dx\). Replacing \(x \to \tfrac{\pi}{2}-x\) swaps \(\sin x \leftrightarrow \cos x\), giving \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \dfrac{\cos^{3/2} x}{\cos^{3/2} x + \sin^{3/2} x}\,dx\). Adding, \(2I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} 1\,dx = \tfrac{\pi}{2}\), so \(I = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\).

Let \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \dfrac{\cos^5 x}{\sin^5 x + \cos^5 x}\,dx\). Replacing \(x \to \tfrac{\pi}{2}-x\) swaps \(\sin x \leftrightarrow \cos x\), giving \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \dfrac{\sin^5 x}{\cos^5 x + \sin^5 x}\,dx\). Adding, \(2I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} 1\,dx = \tfrac{\pi}{2}\), so \(I = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\).

Let \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi/4} \log(1+\tan x)\,dx\). Replacing \(x \to \tfrac{\pi}{4}-x\) and using \(\tan\!\left(\tfrac{\pi}{4}-x\right) = \dfrac{1-\tan x}{1+\tan x}\), \(1+\tan\!\left(\tfrac{\pi}{4}-x\right) = \dfrac{2}{1+\tan x}\), so \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi/4}\big(\log 2 - \log(1+\tan x)\big)dx = \tfrac{\pi}{4}\log 2 - I\). Hence \(2I = \tfrac{\pi}{4}\log 2\), so \(I = \dfrac{\pi}{8}\log 2\).

Since \(\sin 2x = 2\sin x\cos x\), the integrand is \(2\log\sin x - \log(2\sin x\cos x) = \log\sin x - \log\cos x - \log 2 = \log\tan x - \log 2\). Thus \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\log\tan x\,dx - \tfrac{\pi}{2}\log 2\). By \(x \to \tfrac{\pi}{2}-x\), \(\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\log\tan x\,dx = \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\log\cot x\,dx = -\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\log\tan x\,dx\), so it equals \(0\). Hence \(I = -\dfrac{\pi}{2}\log 2\).

\(\sin^2 x\) is even, so \(\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\sin^2 x\,dx = 2\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\sin^2 x\,dx\). By the pairing \(x \to \tfrac{\pi}{2}-x\), \(\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\sin^2 x\,dx = \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\cos^2 x\,dx\), and their sum is \(\tfrac{\pi}{2}\), so each is \(\tfrac{\pi}{4}\). Therefore the value is \(2\cdot\tfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\).

Let \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{x\,dx}{1+\sin x}\). By \(\int_{0}^{a} f(x)\,dx = \int_{0}^{a} f(a-x)\,dx\) with \(a=\pi\) (and \(\sin(\pi-x)=\sin x\)), \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{\pi-x}{1+\sin x}\,dx\). Adding, \(2I = \pi\int_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{dx}{1+\sin x}\). Now \(\dfrac{1}{1+\sin x} = \dfrac{1-\sin x}{\cos^2 x} = \sec^2 x - \sec x\tan x\), whose antiderivative \(\tan x - \sec x = -\dfrac{\cos x}{1+\sin x}\) gives \(\int_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{dx}{1+\sin x} = 1-(-1) = 2\). Hence \(2I = 2\pi\), so \(I = \pi\).
\(\sin^7 x\) is an odd function, since \(\sin^7(-x) = -\sin^7 x\). By \(\int_{-a}^{a} f(x)\,dx = 0\) for odd \(f\), \(\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\sin^7 x\,dx = 0\).

Using \(\int_{0}^{2a} f(x)\,dx = 2\int_{0}^{a} f(x)\,dx\) when \(f(2a-x)=f(x)\): here \(a=\pi\) and \(\cos^5(2\pi-x)=\cos^5 x\), so \(\int_{0}^{2\pi}\cos^5 x\,dx = 2\int_{0}^{\pi}\cos^5 x\,dx\). But by \(x \to \pi-x\), \(\cos^5(\pi-x) = -\cos^5 x\), giving \(\int_{0}^{\pi}\cos^5 x\,dx = -\int_{0}^{\pi}\cos^5 x\,dx = 0\). Therefore \(\int_{0}^{2\pi}\cos^5 x\,dx = 0\).

Let \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\sin x - \cos x}{1+\sin x\cos x}\,dx\). Replacing \(x \to \tfrac{\pi}{2}-x\) swaps \(\sin x \leftrightarrow \cos x\): the numerator becomes \(\cos x - \sin x = -(\sin x - \cos x)\) while the denominator \(1+\sin x\cos x\) is unchanged, so \(I = -I\). Hence \(I = 0\).

Let \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi}\log(1+\cos x)\,dx\). By \(x \to \pi-x\), \(\cos(\pi-x)=-\cos x\), so \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi}\log(1-\cos x)\,dx\). Adding, \(2I = \int_{0}^{\pi}\log(1-\cos^2 x)\,dx = \int_{0}^{\pi}\log(\sin^2 x)\,dx = 2\int_{0}^{\pi}\log\sin x\,dx\). Using the standard result \(\int_{0}^{\pi}\log\sin x\,dx = 2\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\log\sin x\,dx = -\pi\log 2\), we get \(2I = -2\pi\log 2\), so \(I = -\pi\log 2\).

Let \(I = \int_{0}^{a}\dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{a-x}}\,dx\). By \(\int_{0}^{a} f(x)\,dx = \int_{0}^{a} f(a-x)\,dx\), \(I = \int_{0}^{a}\dfrac{\sqrt{a-x}}{\sqrt{a-x}+\sqrt{x}}\,dx\). Adding, \(2I = \int_{0}^{a} 1\,dx = a\), so \(I = \dfrac{a}{2}\).

Let \(I = \int_{0}^{a} f(x)g(x)\,dx\). By \(\int_{0}^{a} h(x)\,dx = \int_{0}^{a} h(a-x)\,dx\), \(I = \int_{0}^{a} f(a-x)g(a-x)\,dx\). Since \(f(a-x)=f(x)\), \(I = \int_{0}^{a} f(x)g(a-x)\,dx\). Adding the two expressions, \(2I = \int_{0}^{a} f(x)\big[g(x)+g(a-x)\big]dx = \int_{0}^{a} f(x)\cdot 4\,dx = 4\int_{0}^{a} f(x)\,dx\). Hence \(I = 2\int_{0}^{a} f(x)\,dx\), as required.

Let \(f(x) = x^{17}\cos^4 x\). Since \(x^{17}\) is odd and \(\cos^4 x\) is even, \(f(-x) = (-x)^{17}\cos^4(-x) = -x^{17}\cos^4 x = -f(x)\), so \(f\) is odd. By \(\int_{-a}^{a} f(x)\,dx = 0\) for an odd function, \(\int_{-1}^{1} x^{17}\cos^4 x\,dx = 0\).
